background_notes.fact: For every real s, the multiplier S_t of D004 is an isometry on H^s and is strongly continuous in t. Consequently the exact twisted solution v(t)=S_{-t}u(t) is L2-continuous, e=v-V is L2-continuous, and ||e(t_n)||_2=||u(t_n)-u^n||_2.

grounds.reason: The H^s norm is the weighted square sum of Fourier coefficients.
The Airy multiplier is exp(i t k^3), of modulus one.
u belongs to C([0,T];H^gamma), gamma>0, and v=S_{-t}u.

background_notes.justification: The weighted square sum is unchanged by a unit-modulus factor. For a fixed f in H^s, truncate its square-summable Fourier series: the finite part varies continuously with t, and the norm of the difference on the tail is at most twice the tail norm, uniformly in t. This proves strong continuity. The isometry and the triangle inequality then give continuity for a time-varying continuous u; H^gamma embeds continuously in L2 because its Fourier weights are at least one. Subtract the continuous V. At a grid point e(t_n)=S_{-t_n}(u(t_n)-u^n), so isometry gives the equality.

background_notes.fact: If a continuous nonnegative function q on [0,T] satisfies q(0)=0 and takes a value at least one, there is a first time t*>0 with q(t*)=1, and q(t)<=1 for 0<=t<=t*. On each compact subinterval, its supremum is finite and attained.

grounds.reason: The exact flow starts at the chosen datum g.
The argument considers q(t)=||e(t)||_2 and a hypothetical first hit; its continuity follows from the Fourier continuity calculation recorded in BG001.

background_notes.justification: Continuity at zero keeps q below one initially. If q reaches or exceeds one, the intermediate value theorem makes {t:q(t)=1} nonempty; it is a closed subset of a compact interval and therefore has a least element t*>0. A value above one before t* would, by the intermediate value theorem, force an earlier hit. The extreme value theorem gives finite attained suprema on compact subintervals. These are routine real-variable consequences applied to the already continuous error norm; the block estimate and contradiction themselves are supplied in S002.

background_notes.fact: For C>=1, pstar=23/14>1 and N=max(2,ceil(8C)), C(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4. With delta=min(1,1/(4C(N^2+3))), 0<tau<=delta/2 and 0<=h<=delta, the full E_I coefficient in N010 is <=1/2, and absorption yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3C delta tau^gamma.

grounds.reason: The exact coefficient and forcing term to be absorbed are explicitly given.
C>=1, N, delta, h and tau have the stated ranges and choices.

background_notes.justification: Since N>=8C and N>=1, monotonicity of real powers gives N^(-pstar)<=N^(-1), and 2C/N<=1/4. Also C(N^2 h+h+tau)<=C delta(N^2+3)<=1/4. Moving their sum, at most 1/2, to the left multiplies the other terms by at most two; 2C(h+tau)<=3C delta.

background_notes.fact: For C0>=1, delta>0 and gamma>0, tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4C0))^(1/gamma)) is positive and C0 tau0^gamma<=1/4.

grounds.reason: C0 is a finite maximum with 1 and tau0 is defined by the stated formula.

background_notes.justification: Every entry in the finite minimum is positive. Since tau0<=(1/(4C0))^(1/gamma), monotonicity of positive real powers with exponent gamma>0 and the power laws give tau0^gamma<=1/(4C0). Multiplying by the positive C0 proves the inequality.
